question: Which among the following is the coldest planet in the solar system?
solution:
**The correct answer is 'Uranus.'**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__**

__
 
• **Uranus:**

 
 
• Uranus is the seventh planet from the Sun and has the coldest atmosphere in the Solar System.
 
• Its minimal temperature can drop as low as -224 degrees Celsius (-371 degrees Fahrenheit).
 
• The extreme cold is due to a combination of its distance from the Sun and its peculiar axial tilt, which causes extreme seasonal variations.
 
• Unlike other gas giants, Uranus has a lower internal heat output, contributing further to its cold temperatures.
 
 

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__**

 
• **Mars:**

 
 
• Mars is the fourth planet from the Sun and has a very thin atmosphere, leading to cold temperatures, but not nearly as cold as Uranus.
 
• Average temperatures on Mars range from -125°C (-195°F) at the poles in winter to 20°C (68°F) in the day during summer at the equator.
 
 
 
• **Neptune:**
 
 
• Neptune, the eighth planet from the Sun, is also extremely cold, but slightly warmer than Uranus due to its greater internal heat.
 
• Neptune's atmospheric temperatures can drop to around -214 degrees Celsius (-353 degrees Fahrenheit).
 
 
 
• **Saturn:**
 
 
• Saturn is the sixth planet from the Sun and, while cold, it is warmer than Uranus and Neptune.
 
• Temperatures in Saturn's upper atmosphere are around -178 degrees Celsius (-288 degrees Fahrenheit).
